hook.situation: You are revising a report or short essay. The Korean must show how one sentence follows from another: evidence leads to a conclusion, a contrast limits the claim, and a final sentence synthesizes the argument.
objectives: Choose formal connectors according to sentence relationship, not English translation.
Use report vocabulary such as 근거, 결론, 핵심, 논리, 사례, and 반론 as one argument set.
Keep written connectors and written-register endings consistent in the same paragraph.
hook.whyItMatters: A learner can know every word in a paragraph and still sound weak if the connectors do not match the logic. This chapter teaches the glue that makes formal Korean writing read like an argument instead of a list of sentences.

grammarNotes.title: 따라서 / 그러므로 — Therefore (evidence to conclusion)
grammarNotes.func: These are the written-register connectors for drawing a logical conclusion from what you just said. They mark the jump from a reason or premise to its result, the way English uses 'therefore.' In conversation Koreans say 그래서, but in essays, reports, and articles they switch to 따라서 or 그러므로. Both open a new sentence.

formTable.when: Evidence stated, you give the result (most neutral, the everyday choice in reports and essays)
formTable.ex: 근거가 부족하다. 따라서 결론을 다시 검토해야 한다.

formTable.when: A more deductive 'thus, it follows that'; slightly weightier, common in arguments
formTable.ex: 누구나 실수를 한다. 그러므로 검토가 필요하다.

formTable.when: The casual spoken version you REPLACE in formal writing (shown for contrast)
formTable.ex: 비가 와서 안 갔어 → 비가 왔다. 따라서 가지 않았다.

examples.ko: 이 보고서는 근거가 부족하다. 따라서 결론을 다시 검토해야 한다.
examples.romanization: i bogoseoneun geungeoga bujokhada. ttaraseo gyeolloneul dasi geomtohaeya handa.
examples.en: This report lacks evidence. Therefore the conclusion must be reviewed again.
examples.note: 따라서 opens the sentence and draws the result straight from the stated problem.

examples.ko: 자료의 출처가 분명하지 않다. 그러므로 핵심 근거로 쓰기 어렵다.
examples.romanization: jaryoui chulcheoga bunmyeonghaji anta. geureomeuro haeksim geungeoro sseugi eoryeopda.
examples.en: The source of the material is unclear. Thus it is hard to use as key evidence.
examples.note: 그러므로 signals a firm 'it follows that,' suiting an argument.

examples.ko: 조사 대상이 제한적이다. 따라서 결과를 일반화하기 어렵다.
examples.romanization: josa daesangi jehanjeogida. ttaraseo gyeolgwareul ilbanhwahagi eoryeopda.
examples.en: The sample is limited. Therefore the result is hard to generalize.
examples.note: The limitation comes first, then 따라서 introduces the warranted conclusion.

examples.ko: 수요가 계속 줄고 있다. 그러므로 생산을 늘릴 이유가 없다.
examples.romanization: suyoga gyesok julgo itda. geureomeuro saengsaneul nullil iyuga eopda.
examples.en: Demand keeps falling. Thus there is no reason to raise production.
examples.note: 그러므로 ties a firm conclusion to the trend just described.

keyPoint.label: 따라서 vs 그러므로
keyPoint.body: Both mean 'therefore' and both are formal. 따라서 is the everyday workhorse of reports and essays — neutral and safe. 그러므로 feels a notch more deductive ('it necessarily follows'), so it shines in arguments and reasoning. In ordinary expository writing, default to 따라서; reach for 그러므로 when you want the logic to feel airtight.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 따라서 starts with a tense ㄸ: [tta-ra-seo]. 그러므로 is four light, even syllables [geu-reo-meu-ro] with no tense consonants — don't stress it like English 'therefore.'

drill.instruction: Replace the casual 그래서 with a formal connector (따라서 or 그러므로) to fit an essay.
items: 모든 조건이 같다. ___ 결과도 같아야 한다.
참가자가 늘었다. ___ 더 큰 장소가 필요하다.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English writers tend to splice 'therefore' on with a comma in the middle of a sentence. In formal Korean, 따라서/그러므로 normally start a NEW sentence after a full stop. Hooking it onto the previous clause with a comma reads as a run-on.

grammarNotes.title: 그러나 / 반면에 / 한편 — three kinds of contrast
grammarNotes.func: Formal writing splits into three the contrast that casual 하지만 lumps together. 그러나 directly reverses or limits what you just said ('however'). 반면에 sets two things side by side as opposites ('by contrast, whereas'). 한편 moves to a separate, co-occurring point ('meanwhile, for its part') without contradicting. Picking the right one is a mark of polished writing.

formTable.when: Direct reversal or limitation of the previous claim — the strong written 'however'
formTable.ex: 핵심 주장은 분명하다. 그러나 근거가 부족하다.

formTable.when: Comparing two items as contrasting opposites; often after stating side A
formTable.ex: 첫 사례는 적절하다. 반면에 두 번째 사례는 약하다.

formTable.when: Adding a separate, co-occurring angle or new actor — not a contradiction
formTable.ex: 보고서는 비용을 강조한다. 한편 안전 검토는 부족하다.

examples.ko: 핵심 주장은 분명하다. 그러나 이를 뒷받침할 근거가 부족하다.
examples.romanization: haeksim jujangeun bunmyeonghada. geureona ireul dwitbatchimhal geungeoga bujokhada.
examples.en: The main claim is clear. However, the evidence to support it is insufficient.
examples.note: 그러나 directly limits the positive first sentence.

examples.ko: 첫 번째 사례는 적절하다. 반면에 두 번째 사례는 관련성이 약하다.
examples.romanization: cheot beonjjae saryeneun jeokjeolhada. banmyeone du beonjjae saryeneun gwallyeonseongi yakada.
examples.en: The first case is fitting. By contrast, the second case is weakly relevant.
examples.note: 반면에 lines up two comparable cases as opposites.

examples.ko: 보고서는 비용 문제를 강조한다. 한편 안전 문제 검토는 충분하지 않다.
examples.romanization: bogoseoneun biyong munjereul gangjohanda. hanpyeon anjeon munje geomtoneun chungbunhaji anta.
examples.en: The report stresses the cost issue. Meanwhile, the review of safety is not sufficient.
examples.note: 한편 shifts to a separate line of discussion, not a flat contradiction.

examples.ko: 이론은 단순하다. 그러나 적용은 결코 쉽지 않다.
examples.romanization: ironeun dansunhada. geureona jeogyongeun gyeolko swipji anta.
examples.en: The theory is simple. However, applying it is by no means easy.
examples.note: 그러나 flags a sharp 'but in reality' reversal, stronger than 하지만.

keyPoint.label: 그러나 vs 반면에 vs 한편
keyPoint.body: Test by relationship: if B cancels or limits A, use 그러나 (however). If B is the mirror-opposite of A, weighed against it, use 반면에 (by contrast). If B is just a separate development from another side, use 한편 (meanwhile). A common error is using 한편 where 반면에 is needed — 한편 does NOT mean 'in contrast,' it means 'from another quarter, at the same time.'

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 반면에 is [ban-myeo-ne] — the ㄴ of 면 links into 에, so it flows as one word, not 반/면/에 chopped apart. 한편 is [han-pyeon].

drill.instruction: Choose 그러나, 반면에, or 한편 for the contrast type shown in brackets.
drill.model: 가격은 올랐다. ___ 판매량은 그대로다. [two opposites compared] → 반면에
items: 모두 찬성할 줄 알았다. ___ 반대가 거셌다. [direct reversal]
서울은 비가 왔다. ___ 부산은 맑았다. [two opposites compared]
연구진은 실험을 이어갔다. ___ 학계는 논쟁을 벌였다. [separate co-occurring angle]

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 한편, 이 방법은 비싸다. (intending 'however, this method is expensive')
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners map 한편 to 'however' because dictionaries gloss it as 'on the other hand.' But 한편 means 'meanwhile, from another side,' not rebuttal. To overturn a claim use 그러나; to weigh two opposites use 반면에. Using 한편 for a flat contradiction confuses Korean readers.

grammarNotes.title: 즉 / 다시 말해서 — that is, in other words (restate, don't add)
grammarNotes.func: These connectors signal that what follows is a RESTATEMENT or clarification of what you just said — not new information. 즉 is a compact written 'namely, that is,' used to pin down a precise equivalent or definition. 다시 말해서 ('to put it again, in other words') reframes the whole idea in plainer words. Both tell the reader: same point, said more clearly.

formTable.when: Pinpointing an exact equivalent or narrower meaning — terse, very written 'namely, that is'
formTable.ex: 핵심 변수, 즉 가격이 결과를 좌우한다.

formTable.when: Rephrasing the whole idea in plainer words for the reader
formTable.ex: 수요가 공급을 넘었다. 다시 말해서, 물건이 부족하다.

formTable.when: Shorter written variant of 다시 말해서, often before a clause
formTable.ex: 비용이 효용을 넘는다. 다시 말해 손해다.

examples.ko: 문제는 결론 자체가 아니다. 즉, 근거와 논리의 연결이 약하다는 점이다.
examples.romanization: munjeneun gyeollon jachega anida. jeuk, geungeowa nolliui yeongyeori yakadaneun jeomida.
examples.en: The problem is not the conclusion itself. That is, the link between evidence and reasoning is weak.
examples.note: 즉 restates the diagnosis in a more precise form, adding no new fact.

examples.ko: 이 문장은 너무 추상적이다. 다시 말해서, 독자가 떠올릴 사례가 없다.
examples.romanization: i munjangeun neomu chusangjeogida. dasi malhaeseo, dokjaga tteoolril saryega eopda.
examples.en: This sentence is too abstract. In other words, there is no example the reader can picture.
examples.note: 다시 말해서 reframes the abstract point in concrete, plainer terms.

examples.ko: 가장 중요한 요소, 즉 신뢰가 무너졌다.
examples.romanization: gajang jungyohan yoso, jeuk silloega muneojyeotda.
examples.en: The most important element — namely, trust — collapsed.
examples.note: 즉 equates the abstract 'most important element' with the concrete word 신뢰; it sits inside the sentence.

examples.ko: 지출이 수입을 넘었다. 다시 말해, 적자가 났다.
examples.romanization: jichuri suibeul neomeotda. dasi malhae, jeokjaga natda.
examples.en: Spending exceeded income. In other words, there was a deficit.
examples.note: 다시 말해 (the shorter form) restates the situation with its plain name.

keyPoint.label: 즉 vs 다시 말해서
keyPoint.body: 즉 is for a tight, near-mathematical equivalence ('X, namely Y') and often sits INSIDE a sentence right after the term it defines. 다시 말해서 is for rephrasing a whole idea more accessibly and usually starts a fresh sentence. Rule of thumb: 즉 swaps in a precise synonym; 다시 말해서 explains the same point again in different words. Neither one introduces new evidence — for that, use 또한 or 예를 들어.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 즉 is one tight syllable [jeuk], ending in a hard ㄱ stop. 다시 말해서 is [da-si mal-hae-seo], even and unstressed.

drill.instruction: Insert 즉 or 다시 말해서 so the second sentence restates (not adds to) the first.
drill.model: 이 글은 사례가 없다. ___ 추상적이다. → 다시 말해서
items: 문제는 결론이 아니다. ___ 근거가 약하다는 점이다.
매출은 늘었지만 이익은 줄었다. ___ 효율이 떨어졌다.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 근거가 약하다. 즉, 새로운 사례를 하나 더 들 수 있다.
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 근거가 약하다. 즉, 주장을 뒷받침하기 어렵다.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners use 즉 like a loose English 'so' and then add a brand-new point. But 즉 only RESTATES what was already said in a clearer form. If you are adding new evidence, use 또한 or 예를 들어; if a result follows, use 따라서.

grammarNotes.title: 결국 / 궁극적으로 — final synthesis (what it all comes to)
grammarNotes.func: These pull a chain of reasoning together and name the final point. 결국 means 'in the end, ultimately' — the result or conclusion reached after a process. 궁극적으로 is 'ultimately, fundamentally,' a touch more abstract and principle-like. They are not just 'finally' (which only marks the last item in time); they answer what everything has been leading to.

formTable.when: Summing up the result after a process or chain of points
formTable.ex: 여러 자료를 검토했지만 결국 같은 결론에 도달했다.

formTable.when: Stating the deepest, most general principle behind it all
formTable.ex: 궁극적으로 좋은 글은 주장과 근거가 연결되어야 한다.

formTable.when: Marking an awaited event that finally happens (NOT synthesis — contrast only)
formTable.ex: 드디어 보고서를 제출했다. (at last — not a conclusion)

examples.ko: 결국 이 보고서의 핵심은 결론을 바꾸는 것이 아니라 근거를 보완하는 것이다.
examples.romanization: gyeolguk i bogoseoui haeksimeun gyeolloneul bakkuneun geosi anira geungeoreul bowanhaneun geosida.
examples.en: Ultimately, the key point of this report is not to change the conclusion but to strengthen the evidence.
examples.note: 결국 gathers the whole discussion and names the real takeaway.

examples.ko: 궁극적으로 좋은 글은 주장, 근거, 반론이 서로 연결되어야 한다.
examples.romanization: gunggeukjeogeuro joeun geureun jujang, geungeo, balloni seoro yeongyeoldoeeoya handa.
examples.en: Ultimately, good writing requires the claim, evidence, and counterargument to connect.
examples.note: 궁극적으로 sounds broader and more principle-like than 결국.

examples.ko: 여러 자료를 검토했지만 결국 같은 결론에 도달했다.
examples.romanization: yeoreo jaryoreul geomtohaetjiman gyeolguk gateun gyeollone dochakhaetda.
examples.en: Several sources were reviewed, but in the end they reached the same conclusion.
examples.note: 결국 marks the final result after the process of reviewing.

examples.ko: 논의는 길었다. 그러나 결국 핵심은 하나였다.
examples.romanization: nonuineun gireotda. geureona gyeolguk haeksimeun hanayeotda.
examples.en: The discussion was long. However, in the end the key point was just one.
examples.note: 결국 closes a long buildup by naming the single point it all reduces to.

keyPoint.label: 결국 vs 궁극적으로 vs 드디어
keyPoint.body: 결국 names the result a process arrives at ('in the end'). 궁극적으로 names the deepest principle behind everything ('fundamentally, ultimately'), so it fits broad closing statements. Neither is 드디어, which only means an awaited event 'finally' happened — a time word, not a synthesis. Save 결국/궁극적으로 for a real summary; don't open every paragraph with them.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 결국 is [gyeol-guk], two syllables both ending in a hard stop. 궁극적으로 is [gung-geuk-jeo-geu-ro], five even syllables — keep it steady, don't rush the middle.

drill.instruction: Fill the blank with 결국 or 드디어 by meaning: synthesis-of-a-process vs awaited-event-at-last.
drill.model: 오래 기다린 끝에 ___ 결과가 나왔다. → 드디어
items: 여러 안을 비교했지만 ___ 첫 안으로 돌아왔다.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 오래 준비한 발표를 결국 끝냈다. (intending 'I finally finished it!')
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English 'finally' covers both 'at long last' and 'in conclusion,' so learners reach for 결국 for an awaited relief. But 결국 carries a result-of-a-process nuance (often a slightly resigned 'in the end'). For the happy 'at last' sense, use 드디어.

grammarNotes.title: Written endings — -다 / -ㄴ다·-는다 / -이다
grammarNotes.func: Formal connectors need formal endings around them. If a paragraph uses 따라서 but then ends every sentence in -해요, the logic sounds written but the voice sounds conversational. In expository Korean (essays, reports, articles) you use the plain written style: adjectives and the copula in -다, action verbs in -ㄴ다/-는다, and noun statements in -이다. This is the register that pairs with the connectors in this chapter.

formTable.when: Adjective or descriptive verb (the plain dictionary -다 carries the written meaning)
Action verb in expository prose — vowel stem +-ㄴ다, consonant stem +-는다
formTable.ex: 필자는 비용 문제를 강조한다. / 자료를 충분히 다루지 않는다.

examples.ko: 이 글은 사례가 부족하다. 따라서 설득력이 약하다.
examples.romanization: i geureun saryega bujokhada. ttaraseo seoldeungnyeogi yakada.
examples.en: This piece lacks examples. Therefore it is not very persuasive.
examples.note: Both sentences keep the plain written -다 on adjectives.

examples.ko: 필자는 비용 문제를 강조한다. 그러나 안전 문제는 충분히 다루지 않는다.
examples.romanization: piljaneun biyong munjereul gangjohanda. geureona anjeon munjeneun chungbunhi daruji anneunda.
examples.en: The writer stresses cost. However, the safety issue is not treated sufficiently.
examples.note: Action verbs in formal writing take -ㄴ다/-는다, not -해요.

examples.ko: 핵심은 자료의 양이 아니라 관련성이다.
examples.romanization: haeksimeun jaryoui yangi anira gwallyeonseongida.
examples.en: The key point is not the amount of material but its relevance.
examples.note: Noun conclusions take -이다.

examples.ko: 결국 좋은 글은 근거와 사례가 연결되어야 한다.
examples.romanization: gyeolguk joeun geureun geungeowa saryega yeongyeoldoeeoya handa.
examples.en: Ultimately, good writing requires evidence and cases to connect.
examples.note: -아야 한다 keeps the obligation in plain written style, matching 결국.

keyPoint.label: One register per paragraph
keyPoint.body: Decide the register first, then keep it. Expository writing uses the plain written style: adjectives/copula in -다·-이다 and action verbs in -ㄴ다/-는다. -습니다 is also formal and fits presentations and polite reports — but pick one. Mixing -해요 with academic connectors like 따라서 and 즉 makes a single paragraph feel stylistically uneven, even when every word is correct.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: -ㄴ다/-는다 endings end on a clean -다 [da]; don't soften them toward the spoken -다아. -이다 is [i-da], the 이 fully voiced after a consonant.

drill.instruction: Rewrite each -해요 sentence in plain written style (adjective/noun → -다/-이다, action verb → -ㄴ다/-는다).

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners default to the safe spoken -해요 even after a written connector like 따라서. In an essay or report this clashes: the connector says 'formal writing,' the ending says 'conversation.' Match the ending to the register — use -다/-ㄴ다/-는다/-이다 throughout the paragraph.

exampleSentence.en: Evidence that supports the claim must be presented.
exampleSentence.note: Use 근거 when a claim needs support, not merely a reason.

exampleSentence.en: If the evidence is weak, the conclusion also loses persuasiveness.
exampleSentence.note: 결론 is the endpoint of reasoning, not a story ending.

exampleSentence.ko: 이 글의 핵심은 비용 문제가 아니라 안전 문제이다.
exampleSentence.en: The key point of this piece is not cost but safety.
exampleSentence.note: 핵심 narrows attention to the central issue.

exampleSentence.en: The claim is clear, but there is a leap in the reasoning.
exampleSentence.note: Say 논리에 비약이 있다, not 논리가 비약하다.

exampleSentence.ko: 주장을 뒷받침하려면 구체적인 사례를 제시해야 한다.
exampleSentence.en: To support a claim, concrete cases must be presented.
exampleSentence.note: 사례 is more formal and analytical than 예.

exampleSentence.en: However, expected counterarguments must also be reviewed.
exampleSentence.note: A strong formal paragraph anticipates objections.

exampleSentence.ko: 자료의 출처가 분명하지 않다. 따라서 핵심 근거로 사용하기 어렵다.
exampleSentence.en: The source of the material is unclear. Therefore, it is difficult to use as key evidence.
exampleSentence.note: 따라서 connects evidence to a formal consequence.

exampleSentence.ko: 핵심 주장은 분명하다. 그러나 근거가 부족하다.
exampleSentence.en: The main claim is clear. However, the evidence is insufficient.
exampleSentence.note: 그러나 gives a direct formal contrast.

exampleSentence.ko: 첫 번째 사례는 적절하다. 반면에 두 번째 사례는 관련성이 약하다.
exampleSentence.en: The first case is appropriate. By contrast, the second case is weakly relevant.

exampleSentence.ko: 문제는 결론 자체가 아니다. 즉, 근거와 논리의 연결이 약하다는 점이다.
exampleSentence.en: The problem is not the conclusion itself. In other words, the link between evidence and reasoning is weak.
exampleSentence.note: 즉 clarifies the same point in a narrower form.

exampleSentence.ko: 결국 좋은 보고서는 주장, 근거, 사례가 서로 연결되어야 한다.
exampleSentence.en: Ultimately, a good report requires its claim, evidence, and cases to be connected.
exampleSentence.note: 결국 summarizes what the whole discussion leads to.

extendedDialogue.setting: Two classmates are revising a Korean report draft before submission.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Therefore, the conclusion must be reviewed again.
lines.grammarNote: 따라서 links the diagnosis to the required action.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 그러나 핵심 주장은 유지할 수 있습니다.
lines.romanization: geureona haeksim jujangeun yujihal su itseumnida.
lines.en: However, the main claim can be maintained.
lines.grammarNote: 그러나 limits the criticism so the whole argument is not rejected.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: By contrast, the case analysis needs strengthening.
lines.grammarNote: 반면에 compares one part of the report with another.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 한편 예상되는 반론도 따로 검토해야 합니다.
lines.romanization: hanpyeon yesangdoeneun ballondo ttaro geomtohaeya hamnida.
lines.en: Meanwhile, the expected counterarguments also need to be reviewed separately.
lines.grammarNote: 한편 opens a related but parallel issue.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 즉, 결론보다 근거와 논리를 보완해야 합니다.
lines.romanization: jeuk, gyeollonboda geungeowa nollireul bowanhaeya hamnida.
lines.en: In other words, the evidence and reasoning need more work than the conclusion.
lines.grammarNote: 즉 restates the revision target more clearly.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 결국 보고서는 주장, 근거, 사례가 서로 연결되어야 합니다.
lines.romanization: gyeolguk bogoseoneun jujang, geungeo, saryega seoro yeongyeoldoeeoya hamnida.
lines.en: Ultimately, a report's claim, evidence, and cases must be connected.

readingText.title: 근거가 부족한 보고서 고치기
readingText.body: 초안 보고서는 결론이 분명했으나 근거가 부족했다. 따라서 결론을 유지하되 사례 분석을 보완해야 한다. 그러나 모든 내용을 새로 쓸 필요는 없다. 핵심 주장은 유지할 수 있다. 반면에 반론 검토는 아직 약하다. 즉, 문제는 결론 자체가 아니라 근거와 논리의 연결이다. 결국 좋은 보고서는 주장, 근거, 사례, 반론이 서로 연결될 때 설득력을 가진다.
readingText.bodyTranslation: The draft report had a clear conclusion, but the evidence was insufficient. Therefore, the conclusion can remain, but the case analysis needs to be strengthened. However, not all content needs to be rewritten. The main claim can be kept. By contrast, the counterargument review is still weak. In other words, the problem is not the conclusion itself but the link between evidence and reasoning. Ultimately, a good report is persuasive when claim, evidence, cases, and counterarguments are connected.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 초안 보고서의 가장 큰 문제는 무엇인가요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 결론 자체가 아니라 근거와 논리의 연결이 약한 것입니다.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 왜 따라서가 쓰였나요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 근거가 부족하다는 진단에서 사례 분석을 보완해야 한다는 결론이 이어지기 때문입니다.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 글의 마지막 문장에서 결국은 어떤 역할을 하나요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 앞의 수정 방향을 모아 좋은 보고서의 조건으로 정리합니다.

culturalNote.title: Formal Korean writing is relationship logic
culturalNote.body: Korean essays and reports often sound polished because each connector tells the reader exactly how to process the next sentence. 그러나 does not merely mean 'but'; it tells the reader to revise the previous claim. 즉 does not merely mean 'so'; it tells the reader to reinterpret the same point more precisely.
culturalNote.tip: Before choosing a connector, name the relationship in Korean: 결론, 대조, 비교, 보충, 재진술, or 종합.

inlineExercises.prompt: 근거가 부족하다. ___ 결론을 다시 검토해야 한다.
inlineExercises.explanation: The second sentence is a consequence of the first.

inlineExercises.prompt: 첫 번째 사례는 적절하다. ___ 두 번째 사례는 관련성이 약하다.
inlineExercises.explanation: Two comparable sides are being contrasted.

inlineExercises.prompt: 문제는 결론이 아니다. ___ 근거와 논리의 연결이 약하다는 점이다.
inlineExercises.explanation: The second sentence restates the diagnosis more precisely.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence keeps written register most consistently?
options: 결국 좋은 글은 근거와 사례가 연결되어야 한다.
결국 좋은 글은 근거랑 사례가 연결돼요.
결국 좋은 글은 근거랑 사례, 이런 게 중요해요.
inlineExercises.correct: 결국 좋은 글은 근거와 사례가 연결되어야 한다.
inlineExercises.explanation: 결국 plus -다 style keeps the paragraph formal and written.
부족하다 describes the evidence, so 근거 takes 가. 를 would make evidence an object, which does not fit this adjective.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'The evidence is weak. Therefore, the conclusion must be reviewed.'
inlineExercises.correct: 근거가 약하다. 따라서 결론을 다시 검토해야 한다.
inlineExercises.explanation: 따라서 connects evidence to a conclusion or required action. The written ending -다 keeps the register consistent.

inlineExercises.prompt: Restate with “that is”: 문제는 결론이 아니다. ___ 근거와 논리의 연결이다.
inlineExercises.explanation: 즉 restates or clarifies the same point. It should not introduce an unrelated new contrast.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the written-register mismatch: '근거가 약하다 ㅋㅋ 따라서 다시 검토해야 한다.'
inlineExercises.correct: 근거가 약하다. 따라서 다시 검토해야 한다.
inlineExercises.explanation: ㅋㅋ belongs to casual chat, not a formal written paragraph. Removing it keeps the report register consistent.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which connector best contrasts two cases?
inlineExercises.explanation: 반면에 contrasts two sides or cases. 즉 restates, and 따라서 draws a conclusion.
궁극적으로 gives final synthesis. -이다 keeps the written-register ending consistent.

bullets: 따라서: evidence or condition leads to a conclusion.
그러나: direct limitation or reversal. 반면에: two-sided comparison. 한편: related parallel development.
즉: restatement or clarification, not new evidence.
결국: final synthesis after a chain of reasoning.
근거, 결론, 핵심, 논리, 사례, 반론 belong together in report and essay revision.

writingTask.prompt: Write a short expository paragraph (3-4 sentences) arguing a point, using formal written connectors and consistent written endings.
writingTask.hint: Use 따라서/그러므로 for the conclusion, 그러나/반면에 for contrast, 즉/다시 말해서 to restate, and written endings -다 / -ㄴ다·-는다 / -이다 throughout (not 해요).
writingTask.model: 운동은 건강에 중요하다. 그러나 시간이 없는 사람이 많다. 따라서 짧게라도 매일 걷는 것이 좋다. 즉, 운동은 길이보다 꾸준함이 핵심이다.
writingTask.modelEn: Exercise is important for health. However, many people have no time. Therefore, it is good to walk every day, even briefly. That is, for exercise, consistency rather than length is the key.

canDo: Draw a conclusion in formal writing with 따라서 / 그러므로 (따라서 …다)
Distinguish three kinds of contrast with 그러나 / 반면에 / 한편
Restate without adding new information using 즉 / 다시 말해서 (즉, …이다)
Keep a consistent written register with -다 / -ㄴ다·-는다 / -이다 endings (and 결국/궁극적으로 to synthesize)
